note.en: What you see: With a full bladder as the window, the bladder appears as a large dark oval above the pubic bone. Behind it in men lies the rectovesical pouch and behind the uterus in women lies the pouch of Douglas, the lowest peritoneal recess where free fluid collects. In health the organs hug each other with no dark stripe behind the bladder. An empty bladder folds the recess shut and hides fluid, so bladder filling decides whether this view can be trusted.

label.en: Urinary bladder, rectovesical pouch in men, pouch of Douglas in women.

note.en: Landmarks to confirm: Urinary bladder, rectovesical pouch in men, pouch of Douglas in women.

steps.en: What you see: With a full bladder as the window, the bladder appears as a large dark oval above the pubic bone. Behind it in men lies the rectovesical pouch and behind the uterus in women lies the pouch of Douglas, the lowest peritoneal recess where free fluid collects. In health the organs hug each other with no dark stripe behind the bladder. An empty bladder folds the recess shut and hides fluid, so bladder filling decides whether this view can be trusted.
Landmarks to confirm: Urinary bladder, rectovesical pouch in men, pouch of Douglas in women.

Common mistakes and correction: Empty bladder hiding posterior fluid: fill or wait, then repeat. Bowel gas mimicking fluid behind the bladder: confirm the stripe persists in both transverse and lengthwise planes. Too much pressure collapsing small veins and hiding fluid: lighten the hand and rescan.

Normal values with units: No numeric threshold applies. In health no anechoic stripe lies behind a well filled bladder. Any new dark stripe in the pouch after trauma, or with abdominal pain and a positive pregnancy test, is abnormal and needs urgent senior review.

Pitfalls: In a person of childbearing age with pain and bleeding, fluid in the pouch of Douglas may signal ruptured ectopic pregnancy, so escalate fast. Clotted blood can look bright and mimic bowel, so correlate with the clinical picture. Always scan in two planes before calling the pelvis negative.

todo.en: How to get it step by step: Place the probe on the suprapubic midline in transverse with the marker to the right. Angle down behind the pubic bone until the full bladder oval fills the screen. Sweep down through the base of the bladder to open the pouch behind it. Then turn lengthwise and sweep side to side. If the bladder is empty, wait for natural filling with senior approval, or clamp a catheter already placed for another indication per local protocol, and repeat rather than calling the view negative.

q.en: Why does bladder filling matter in this view?

o.en: An empty bladder gives the clearest view
A full bladder is needed to open the recess

why.en: An empty bladder folds the recess shut and hides fluid, so a full bladder is the window.

q.en: The bladder is empty and no fluid shows. What is correct?

o.en: Call the pelvis negative at once
Press harder to open the pouch
Fill or wait, then repeat the view

why.en: An empty bladder view cannot be trusted, so repeat after filling rather than calling it negative.

q.en: Fluid shows in the pouch of Douglas with pain and bleeding in early pregnancy. What next?

o.en: Escalate fast for possible ruptured ectopic pregnancy

why.en: This pattern may signal ruptured ectopic pregnancy and needs urgent senior review.
